content:
Shah Rukh Khan turned 61 on Monday, November 2, 2026, and marked the day the way only a global movie star can: with new music. The makers of his upcoming action thriller King released the film's first song, “Tu Mil Jaaye,” shortly after midnight, reuniting Khan on screen with Deepika Padukone.

The track pairs Indian playback singer Arijit Singh with British star Ed Sheeran, who contributes an English rap, with Madhubanti Bagchi also featured on vocals. Sachin-Jigar composed the music, Kumaar wrote the Hindi lyrics, and Sheeran penned the English rap, according to reports from Filmfare and Mirchi. The song runs 3 minutes and 42 seconds, Pinkvilla reported, moving between romantic scenes with Khan and Padukone and flashes of the film's action.

Fans gathered outside Khan's Mumbai home, Mannat, a yearly birthday ritual, where a written note from the actor thanking his admirers was posted for them to read. Sharing the song, Khan wrote: “Yeh Daur Ishq ka Naseeb Waalon ko milta hai... Jahan Barood ki Khushboo mein Gulab khilta hai... Of Love and other Battles... This December, #LoveLikeAKing #TuMilJaaye song out now! #KING in cinemas 24.12.26.”

King is directed by Siddharth Anand, reuniting him with Khan after Pathaan, and is produced by Red Chillies Entertainment and Marflix Pictures. The ensemble cast includes Suhana Khan, Abhishek Bachchan, Rani Mukerji, Anil Kapoor, Jackie Shroff, Jaideep Ahlawat and Arshad Warsi, among others. The film is scheduled to arrive in cinemas worldwide on December 24, 2026.

Analysis: Why this birthday drop matters

Last year, Khan's 60th birthday brought the first look from King. This year, the birthday brought the first song — a deliberate escalation from image to music, and one built for sharing. Pairing Singh, one of Bollywood's defining voices, with Sheeran, a global pop star, turns a local birthday moment into an international one, and reuniting Khan and Padukone — one of Hindi cinema's most bankable pairings — gives the song an instant audience on two continents. With a Christmas Eve release date, the song is less a teaser than the starting gun for King's final seven-week sprint to theaters.
